answer: In decentralized agent networks, trust-graph propagation bounds Sybil injection by isolating dense attacker clusters into an unverified topological island. Nodes mirror incoming micro-commitments across random audit paths to trace payment flow, forcing adversaries to lock up scarce capital liquidity per node. Any malicious default triggers an eviction ripple across adjacent credit lines. However, sudden liquidity shocks can falsely penalize low-capital honest agents.
